To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we develop an approach for risk-averse Bayesian optimization with heteroscedastic objectives, which we demonstrate to be effective on synthetic benchmarks and real-world hyperparameter tuning tasks.

(i) we introduce a novel risk-aware heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression model that can be used for black-box optimization tasks in high-stakes settings and (ii) we provide a theoretical regret bound for our approach and demonstrate its effectiveness on synthetic benchmark functions as well as hyperparameter tuning tasks.
we propose a novel heteroscedastic risk-averse BO algorithm (RAH-BO), which optimizes a risk-aware acquisition function that trades mean and variance of the objective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How to make Bayesian optimization more robust and risk-aware?
the development of a risk-averse BO algorithm that optimizes both expected return and noise variance of the objective.
the following questions: How to incorporate risk-awareness into Bayesian optimization? What is the regret bound of the resulting algorithm? How to report the final solution in a risk-aware manner?

the proposed risk-averse hetero-scedastic Bayesian optimization approach is a promising alternative to existing Bayesian optimization methods.
our proposed approach RAHBO is able to achieve a trade-off between the risk-averse and risk-neutral BO, and is capable of identifying solutions with low noise variance.
the proposed approach RAHBO outperforms the state of the art in the majority of the tested problems, while also being more robust to noise in the data.

RAHBO provides an effective and principled approach to risk-averse BO, and is particularly useful in high-stakes settings where risk-aversion is a necessity.
